# GraphicsService

[Framework](README.md) · `DotGame.Framework.Graphics` · class

```csharp
public sealed class GraphicsService
```

Draws: sprite batches, textures, render targets and the scissor. Reach it as `Game.Graphics`.

## Properties

### MultisampleCount

```csharp
public int MultisampleCount { get; }
```

The samples per pixel the screen is drawn with, which the game's options asked for and the device allowed; 1 means none. Render textures always have one.

### ScissorRectangle

```csharp
public RectangleInt? ScissorRectangle { get; }
```

Types: [`RectangleInt`](RectangleInt.md)

The only area drawing can change on the current target, in the coordinates of sprites with no transform, or null for all of it.

### SharedSpriteBatch

```csharp
public SpriteBatch SharedSpriteBatch { get; }
```

Types: [`SpriteBatch`](SpriteBatch.md)

A sprite batch for everyday drawing, so a game needn't make its own.

## Events

### DeviceReset

```csharp
public event EventHandler? DeviceReset;
```

The graphics device was lost and has come back (a mobile GL context, or a web page's). The platform has restored textures and shaders loaded through content. Rebuild anything the game drew itself: a [`RenderTexture`](RenderTexture.md)'s contents are gone.

### ReadPixelsAsync

```csharp
public Task ReadPixelsAsync(RenderTexture renderTexture, Memory<Color32> destination)
```

Types: [`RenderTexture`](RenderTexture.md), [`Color32`](Color32.md)

Reads a render texture's pixels into `destination`, one per texel: RGBA, premultiplied as drawn, the top row first. The pixels are those drawn to the texture so far this frame, once they've been drawn, so the task completes later (on the game thread), when the frame's drawing has run.

| Parameter | |
|---|---|
| `renderTexture` | The texture to read. |
| `destination` | Where the pixels go: at least as many as the texture has. It must stay untouched until the task completes. |

### UseRenderTarget

```csharp
public RenderTargetScope UseRenderTarget(RenderTexture renderTexture)
```

Types: [`RenderTargetScope`](RenderTargetScope.md), [`RenderTexture`](RenderTexture.md)

Draws to a render texture until the returned value is disposed, then goes back to what was being drawn to: `using (Graphics.UseRenderTarget(texture)) { ... }`. These nest, so code drawing to a texture needn't know what its caller was drawing to. A value can also be kept and disposed later, last made first disposed; ending one early ends those made after it.

**Throws `InvalidOperationException`:** A sprite batch is drawing: its [`SpriteBatch.UseRenderTarget`](SpriteBatch.md#userendertarget) changes the target without ending it.

A target starts with no scissor, as a scissor's coordinates are its own target's, and the scissor comes back with the target before it.

### UseScissor

```csharp
public ScissorScope UseScissor(RectangleInt rectangle)
```

Types: [`ScissorScope`](ScissorScope.md), [`RectangleInt`](RectangleInt.md)

Limits drawing to a rectangle until the returned value is disposed, then goes back to the limit before it: `using (Graphics.UseScissor(rectangle)) { ... }`. These nest, and an inner one is limited by the one around it, so code that clips needn't know what its caller clipped to. A value can also be kept and disposed later, last made first disposed; ending one early ends those made after it.

| Parameter | |
|---|---|
| `rectangle` | The area, in the coordinates of sprites with no transform. It ignores any transform, and an empty one, of no positive size, draws nothing. |

It can change during a sprite batch: sprites drawn before the change keep the limit they were drawn with. Each change splits the draw. This one suits a limit fixed on the screen, or one that spans batches. To limit drawing in the coordinates of a batch with a transform, see [`SpriteBatch.UseScissor`](SpriteBatch.md#usescissor).
